This document introduces the overall process for OpenAPI invocation, interface call limitations, and common error codes.

<span id="309f3188"></span>
# Background information

<span id="5aa914e8"></span>
## Invocation methods

Currently, the Intelligent Analysis Agent supports two invocation methods: token and TOP Gateway. The differences between these two methods are as follows:


|Invocation methods |Token invocation |TOP gateway invocation |
|---|---|---|
|Definition |This lightweight invocation method authenticates by including a dedicated token string issued by the platform in the request header, and directly calls the Intelligent Analysis Agent interface. |This standard cloud service invocation method is based on the unified TOP gateway system of BytePlus, and calls the interface after HMAC\-SHA256 signature authentication using Access Key ID and Secret Access Key. |
|Usage scenarios |* Rapid debugging / testing: Quickly verify interface functionality during development without configuring complex signature logic.<br><br>* Lightweight integration scenarios: Small applications, direct front\-end connections, temporary script invocations, with lower authentication security requirements.<br><br>* Internal temporary use: Rapid integration for non\-core enterprise systems or short\-term projects.<br><br>* Low\-code / no\-code platform integration: Quickly integrate without writing signature logic. |* Production invocation in production environments: Stable integration for core enterprise business systems and online services, with higher authentication security.<br><br>* BytePlus ecosystem integration: Scenarios requiring unified authentication with other BytePlus cloud services (such as ECS, VPC, and so on).<br><br>* High\-security scenarios: Services provided externally or invocations involving sensitive data require strict identity verification and permission control.<br><br>* Large\-scale / high\-concurrency invocation: Supports QPS rate limiting and control, suitable for high availability requirements in production environments.<br><br>* Standardized enterprise\-level integration: Complies with the official BytePlus cloud service integration specifications for easier long\-term maintenance. |
|Usage restrictions |None |This method currently only supports the Intelligent Query interface and only supports streaming return results. For supported interfaces, see [Invoke using TOP Gateway](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/dataagent/Invocation_Methods#6fed9ec3). |


<span id="2a86bfad"></span>
## Usage process

<span id="19e4ea22"></span>
### Invoke using token

The overall process is described as follows. For detailed instructions, see below[Method 1: Use JWT Token for invocation](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/dataagent/Invocation_Methods#17fa271c).


1. A ClientID and ClientSecret are generated for each OpenAPI caller, which serve as credentials for invoking the interface.

2. The user uses the ClientID/ClientSecret to call the interface and exchange for a JWT token containing user identity information.

3. When invoking a business interface, the user must include the JWT token in the request header, for example: `Authorization: Bearer jwt_token`.

4. When the interface is invoked, DataAgent verifies the JWT token using a public key and performs rate limiting and auditing.

5. When invoking any DataAgent interface, to facilitate subsequent troubleshooting, it is recommended to add `x-request-id` and `request-id` (ensure the string is unique) to the request headers. Two headers are required because DataAgent consists of multiple components, and different components may use different identifiers. These two parameters will be recorded in the backend logs of DataAgent, providing strong support for analysis and troubleshooting when issues arise, thereby enabling more efficient resolution of potential faults.

6. Return business results.


<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

<span id="a008d47a"></span>
### Invoke using TOP Gateway

The overall process is described as follows. For detailed instructions, see below[Method 2: Use TOP Gateway for invocation](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/dataagent/Invocation_Methods#f3fa14bf).


1. Obtain the Access Key ID (AK) and Secret Access Key (SK) for your BytePlus account.

2. Request the BytePlus TOP Gateway. The gateway will verify the validity of the AK/SK and forward the user identity information to downstream business services.

3. When the interface is invoked, DataAgent must include the AK/SK and complete the **signature** before requesting the TOP Gateway.

4. When invoking any DataAgent interface, to facilitate subsequent troubleshooting, it is recommended to add `x-request-id` and `request-id` (ensure the string is unique) to the request headers. Two headers are required because DataAgent consists of multiple components, and different components may use different identifiers. These two parameters will be recorded in the backend logs of DataAgent, providing strong support for analysis and troubleshooting when issues arise, thereby enabling more efficient resolution of potential failures.

5. The interface returns business results.


<span id="17fa271c"></span>
# Method 1: Use JWT Token for invocation

<span id="382cb893"></span>
## Obtain ClientID and ClientSecret


1. In the Intelligent Analysis Agent service, click the top **Open Platform**, go to the **Developer Console**, and click the **Credential Management** tab on the left.

2. Click **Create Credential**, select the credential type, and set it for a user or for the system (system credentials can only be set by system administrators).

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/57e85794c26548cd8e84058f76b74a5f~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

3. After creation, copy the `ClientID` and `ClientSecret` you obtained.

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/f36a0508e33046ed883131c73eba2ecf~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">warning   </div>
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-wrapper-indent="1">Ensure that <code>ClientID</code> and <code>ClientSecret</code> are kept confidential and managed properly. These are credentials for invoking the interface. Exposure to other users may result in data leakage risks.   </div>
   

<span id="3ff6d57e"></span>
## Request description

Request URL: The interface URL used for invocation varies by environment.

For the BytePlus SaaS environment, the access URL is `https://console.volcengine.com/bi/datawind`, so the interface URL prefix is `https://console.volcengine.com/bi/datawind/aeolus`.

<span id="e6a9dceb"></span>
### Request example

```JSON
# Replace clientId and clientSecret
curl --location --request POST 'https://console.volcengine.com/bi/datawind/aeolus/api/v3/openapi/jwtToken' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
# Note that the region here should be consistent with the region where the account is located, and the available values are: cn-shanghai、cn-beijing
-H "x-vedi-region: cn-shanghai" \
-d '{
  "metadata": {
    "clientId": "{clientId}",
    "clientSecret": "{clientSecret}",
    "proxyUser": "abc****@21**********",
    "expire": 3600
  }
}'
```


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">You can also directly copy the relevant request parameters provided below the credential on the credential management page in the developer console. You only need to replace the obtained ClientID and ClientSecret; the system has already filled in the proxyUser and expire parameters for you.</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip"><img src="https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/9ed2422b6fed43e59e52de3e8733957e~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image" width="2912px" /></div>


<span id="9a97fd45"></span>
### Request parameters


|Name |Type |Required |Example value |Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x\-vedi\-region |string |Optional |cn\-shanghai |The region where the account is located. The value can be: cn\-shanghai, cn\-beijing.<br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div><br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">Ensure that the value here matches the region where the account is located to ensure the SaaS environment can be called successfully.</div><br> |
|clientId |integer |Required |123abc |Login credential ID. For details on how to obtain it, see [Obtain ClientID and ClientSecret](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/dataagent/Invocation_Methods#382cb893). |
|clientSecret |integer |Required |123abc |Login credential secret. For details on how to obtain it, see [Obtain ClientID and ClientSecret](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/dataagent/Invocation_Methods#382cb893). |
|proxyUser |string |Optional |user_1 |The username corresponding to the token. |
|expire |integer |Optional |3600 |Token expiration time. The default value is 3600, in seconds.<br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning" data-tips-is-title="true">warning</div><br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="warning">The maximum token expiration time is <strong>3 days</strong>, that is, 259200.</div><br> |


<span id="bbc076b9"></span>
### Response parameters


|Parameters |Type |Description |
|---|---|---|
|code |string |Return status code. If the request is successful, returns aeolus/ok. The following are error codes and their explanations:<br><br><br>* aeolus/openapiClient/tokenExpired: The token has expired.<br><br>* aeolus/openapiClient/tokenError: The token is incorrect.<br><br>* aeolus/openapiClient/requestRateExcess: Token invocation exceeds the frequency limit.<br><br>* aeolus/openapiClient/blocked: The request has been blocked. |
|data |object |Contains specific information returned by the interface. This includes jwtToken and proxyUser. |
|data.jwtToken |string |Represents the user's identity information. When calling business interfaces, the user needs to include jwtToken in the request header. |
|data.proxyUser |string |The username corresponding to the token. |
|msg |string |A natural language description of the operation result. |


<span id="6ff7ce7b"></span>
### Response example

```JSON
{
    "code": "aeolus/ok",
    "data": {
        "jwtToken": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.ey*****************************************************************************************************************************************************************************.********************-*************************************************************************************-****************************************************************************************************************************-***-********************************************-******************************************************-*************************-****************************************************************************-************-*************************************-*********************************************************************************************************************************************************-****************-******************5sus",
        "proxyUser": "user_1"
    },
    "msg": "成功" //which means "success"
}
```


<span id="e94c7853"></span>
## Use Token for invocation

When invoking the interface, you need to include the jwtToken in the request header, for example: `Authorization: Bearer jwt_token`

The following is an example of using curl to invoke the current user API:

```sql
curl -X GET 'https://{domain}/aeolus/api/v3/open/misc/current_user' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer jwt_token'
# Note that the region here should be consistent with the region where the account is located, 
# and the available values are: cn-shanghai、cn-beijing
-H "x-vedi-region: cn-shanghai" \
```


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>



* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">In the link above, <code>{domain}</code> refers to the environment domain name. For the BytePlus SaaS environment, the interface address prefix is <code>https://console.volcengine.com/bi/datawind</code>.</div>


* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">clientId is not interoperable across different environments.</div>



<span id="f3fa14bf"></span>
# Method 2: Use TOP Gateway for invocation

<span id="67b6bff9"></span>
## Obtain access keys

Before using TOP Gateway to invoke the API, you need to obtain your account's Access Key ID and Secret Access Key. For details, see [Access Key (Key) Management](https://www.volcengine.com/docs/6291/65568?lang=zh).

<span id="7ef153b9"></span>
## API signature configuration

The API signature is used to verify the identity of the requester and prevent tampering of requests. Before invocation, configure according to the BytePlus signature mechanism. For specific methods, see [Signature Method](https://www.volcengine.com/docs/6369/67269?lang=zh).

<span id="6fed9ec3"></span>
## Invoke using TOP Gateway

You can use tools as needed to call the API. It is recommended to use the SDK.

Examples of GET and POST requests are as follows:

```Bash
# Intelligent WenShu
POST https://open.volcengineapi.com?Action=InnerDataAgentDataQueryAdaQuery&Version=2025-05-13
# Get intelligent agent list
GET https://open.volcengineapi.com?Action=InnerDataAgentGetAgentList&Version=2025-05-13
```


When invoking, you must include region information in the Header. Either one is acceptable:

```Bash
# Beijing region
x-vedi-region: cn-beijing
# Shanghai region
x-vedi-region: cn-shanghai 
```


<span id="18f63cb6"></span>
# Interface invocation limits

To ensure service stability and prevent malicious attacks, the DataAgent backend uses the following methods to limit requests:


1. Rate limiting (the interface can currently handle a high volume of external requests; if this still does not meet your needs, you can contact the BytePlus technical support team to request an increase);

2. Blocking, used to reserve some APIs that are not open or temporarily block abnormal requests from users;

3. Audit: Every OpenAPI invocation is recorded, including the caller, interface, parameters, and invocation time.
